assumptions: H_in and H_out are separable Hilbert spaces
I is an arbitrary nonempty set
rho_i is a normal state on B(H_in) and sigma_i is a normal state on B(H_out) for every i in I
exact_candidate.claim: There exists one normal CPTP entanglement-breaking map Lambda attaining inf_{Gamma normal CPTP EB} sup_{i in I} (1/2)||Gamma(rho_i)-sigma_i||_1.
scope_notes: No countability or finite-capacity assumption is in the attainment candidate.
Finite-capacity families are said to permit finite-outcome approximation, but a finite-outcome optimizer is not asserted.
The literature comparison does not verify either candidate claim.

historical_importance: Would extend the finite-dimensional uniform Le Cam/quantum deficiency existence theorem to a constrained class of normal EB channels in separable infinite dimensions and handle output mass escaping to infinity.

strongest_prior_work.source: M. E. Shirokov, Compactness criterion for families of quantum operations in the strong convergence topology and its applications, arXiv:2307.13694v1
strongest_prior_work.statement: Corollary 1A: a closed family of operations/channels is compact in pointwise trace-norm topology iff the outputs of one faithful input state form a trace-norm compact family; Corollary 2 gives the relative-compactness version.
strongest_prior_work.location: PDF pp. 4-8; especially Corollary 1A p. 6, Corollary 2 and Remark 3 p. 7.
strongest_prior_work.relation: Closest compactness theorem, but trace-norm tightness is not supplied by a bounded worst-state loss. It does not cover the candidate weak-star TNI limit and trace repair.

strongest_prior_work.source: M. E. Shirokov, The Schmidt number and partially entanglement breaking channels in infinite dimensions, arXiv:1110.4363v3
strongest_prior_work.statement: For separable Hilbert spaces, the class P_1 of EB channels is closed and convex in the strong convergence topology. Corollary 2 exhibits EB channels for which every Kraus representation has only infinite-rank Kraus operators.
strongest_prior_work.location: PDF p. 10 for strong closure; pp. 12-13 for the Kraus obstruction.
strongest_prior_work.relation: Strong closure does not establish closure of EB TNI maps under pointwise sigma(T,K) convergence. The Kraus theorem shows finite-outcome EB channels are a strict subclass, not that an optimizer fails to be finite-outcome.

strongest_prior_work.source: A. S. Holevo, Entanglement-breaking channels in infinite dimensions, arXiv:0802.0235v1
strongest_prior_work.statement: An EB channel on separable Hilbert spaces admits a Borel measurement-prepare integral representation over a complete separable metric outcome space.
strongest_prior_work.location: PDF p. 2, equation (2); Theorem 1 p. 5 describes a continuous/densely-defined rank-one Kraus analogue.
strongest_prior_work.relation: Establishes the normal EB structure and general outcome space; no minimax attainment or finite-outcome approximation bound is stated.

strongest_prior_work.source: Anna Jenčová, Comparison of quantum channels and statistical experiments, arXiv:1512.07016v2
strongest_prior_work.statement: For finite-dimensional quantum experiments with arbitrary common parameter set, Theorem 4 equates decision/guessing comparison with a single CPTP map satisfying a uniform state trace-norm error bound; the channel-deficiency infimum is attained by compactness.
strongest_prior_work.location: PDF p. 3 states finite-dimensional scope; deficiency definition p. 11; Theorem 4 pp. 18-20.
strongest_prior_work.relation: Exact finite-dimensional predecessor; all channels are optimized there and the Hilbert-space scope excludes the candidate infinite-dimensional case.

strongest_prior_work.source: Yui Kuramochi, Entanglement-breaking channels with general outcome operator algebras, arXiv:1806.05854v2
strongest_prior_work.statement: Theorem 2 characterizes EB maps through QC domination, measurement-prepare form, and compatibility; Theorem 4 proves upper and lower Dedekind-closedness of randomization-equivalence classes of normal EB channels with fixed input von Neumann algebra.
strongest_prior_work.relation: Order completeness is not topological compactness or attainment of a trace-distance minimax objective.

concrete_candidate_mechanism: Extract a minimizing sequence of normal EB CPTP maps in pointwise sigma(T(H_out),K(H_out)) topology; obtain a normal CP TNI EB limit Lambda_0; use liminf ||Lambda_n(rho_i)-sigma_i||_1 >= ||Lambda_0(rho_i)-sigma_i||_1 + 1-Tr(Lambda_0(rho_i)); then add the escaped effect D=I-Lambda_0^*(I) to one fixed prepared normal state tau via X -> Tr(DX)tau. This repair is a single EB channel and the triangle inequality does not increase any indexed loss.
load_bearing_missing_lemma: Prove that the relevant pointwise weak-star limit of normal EB CPTP maps is a normal CP trace-nonincreasing EB map, with EB defined for subchannels and with no hidden tightness or countability assumption. The exact trace-defect liminf inequality must also be proved in the same topology.
compatibility_obligations: The predual limit must be bounded, CP, and trace-nonincreasing, and its Heisenberg adjoint must be normal.
EB must survive the weak-star limit on arbitrary reference extensions, including infinite-dimensional references.
The state-replacement correction must preserve EB and be independent of the index i.
Use half trace distance consistently: the trace-defect term is halved in the objective.
Finite-outcome approximation under a finite Holevo-capacity condition is a separate statement from optimizer attainment.
early_falsification_test: Test the EB-subchannel closure gate directly: seek a sequence of EB channels whose outputs on an entangled input converge weak-star to a positive subnormalized entangled operator. If none exists, prove closure by finite-rank compressions on both systems and trace-norm approximation of the limiting substate. Separately verify the trace-defect liminf inequality on sequences with orthogonal output mass escaping to infinity.
likely_significance_if_fully_established: A dimension-free existence theorem for one common normal EB reconstruction map on arbitrary state families, extending finite-dimensional uniform deficiency attainment and making optimizer existence robust to loss of output mass at infinity.
priority_verdict: UNKNOWN; bounded primary-source pass found nearest antecedents but cannot infer novelty from non-discovery.

finite_outcome_claim.candidate: Finite Holevo capacity permits finite-outcome approximation; finite-outcome attainment is not claimed.
finite_outcome_claim.literature_status: General normal EB maps may need outcomes beyond a finite set, but cited channel-level examples do not decide whether a finite-capacity approximation problem has a finite-outcome optimizer or whether the candidate approximation bound is already known.
